Convert from the congruence–bias parameterisation to native parameters

Source: R/mfd.R
mfd_to_dpars.Rd

Converts from the congruence–bias parameterisation (the midpoint M of the two expected counts, the congruence f, and the source bias delta) to the native parameters (the rates mu, lambdaone, and lambdatwo), and, optionally, converts overdispersions (kappas, kappax, kappaxone, and kappaxtwo) to the native dispersions (shapes, shapexone, and shapextwo). dpars_to_mfd() converts in the other direction.

Usage

mfd_to_dpars(
  M,
  f,
  delta = 0,
  kappas = NULL,
  kappax = NULL,
  kappaxone = NULL,
  kappaxtwo = NULL
)

Arguments

M

Midpoint of the two expected counts: mu + (lambdaone + lambdatwo)/2, equal to (E[y1] + E[y2])/2. Non-negative.

f

Congruence, the mean of the shared component as a proportion of M: mu / M. In [0, 1]. f = 1 means perfect congruence (both exclusive rates are zero); f = 0 means no shared component.

delta

Source bias on the log-ratio scale, 0.5 * log(lambdaone/lambdatwo). 0 is unbiased. +/-Inf is permitted and gives the limit where one exclusive rate is zero.

kappas, kappax

Optional overdispersions on the scale kappa = 1/sqrt(phi), where phi is the NB2 (inverse) dispersion parameter; kappa = 0 is the Poisson limit. kappas is the overdispersion of the shared component. Supplying kappas adds shapes = 1/kappas^2 to the returned list, so kappas = 0 gives shapes = Inf. kappax is one overdispersion for both exclusive components. Supplying kappax adds shapexone and shapextwo to the returned list, both equal to 1/kappax^2. For bipois() and bipois_partialobs(), which have no dispersion parameters, leave every overdispersion argument unset.

kappaxone, kappaxtwo

Optional overdispersions of the two exclusive components, for the general case in which they differ. Supplying them adds shapexone and shapextwo to the returned list. Mutually exclusive with kappax.

Value

A named list of mu, lambdaone, and lambdatwo, with shapes added when kappas is supplied, and shapexone and shapextwo added when kappax, or kappaxone and kappaxtwo, are supplied.

Details

Each argument may be a vector, such as the posterior draws of M, f, and delta. M, f, and delta are recycled to the length of the longest of the three, and any overdispersions to the same length; each element of the returned list is a vector of that length.

To fit a model in the congruence–bias parameterisation, use bf_mfd(), as in vignette("bicountbrms").

See also

dpars_to_mfd(), bipois(), bipois_partialobs(), binegbin(), binegbin_partialobs()

Examples

# A moderately congruent pair, source 1 recording more of the exclusive
# events
mfd_to_dpars(M = 12, f = 0.67, delta = 0.2)
#> $mu
#> [1] 8.04
#> 
#> $lambdaone
#> [1] 4.741606
#> 
#> $lambdatwo
#> [1] 3.178394
#> 

# Perfect congruence: both exclusive rates are zero
mfd_to_dpars(M = 12, f = 1, delta = 0.5)
#> $mu
#> [1] 12
#> 
#> $lambdaone
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $lambdatwo
#> [1] 0
#> 

# kappax: one overdispersion for both exclusive components
mfd_to_dpars(M = 12, f = 0.67, kappas = 0.4, kappax = 0.9)
#> $mu
#> [1] 8.04
#> 
#> $lambdaone
#> [1] 3.96
#> 
#> $lambdatwo
#> [1] 3.96
#> 
#> $shapes
#> [1] 6.25
#> 
#> $shapexone
#> [1] 1.234568
#> 
#> $shapextwo
#> [1] 1.234568
#> 

# kappaxone, kappaxtwo: one overdispersion per exclusive component
mfd_to_dpars(M = 12, f = 0.67, kappas = 0.4,
             kappaxone = 0.9, kappaxtwo = 0.3)
#> $mu
#> [1] 8.04
#> 
#> $lambdaone
#> [1] 3.96
#> 
#> $lambdatwo
#> [1] 3.96
#> 
#> $shapes
#> [1] 6.25
#> 
#> $shapexone
#> [1] 1.234568
#> 
#> $shapextwo
#> [1] 11.11111
#>
